title: Set Up a Separate Work Profile on Your Android Phone
gist: A consumer walkthrough of Android's multi-user feature, which lets a second Google account act as a work profile that keeps apps, notifications, browsing history and files separated on one handset. The guide notes the capability is uneven across OEMs: Pixel supports it, Samsung Galaxy phones do not, offering Secure Folder instead.

themes.theme: Work/personal separation on a single device

insights.claim: Android supports multiple user profiles tied to separate Google accounts, so a single handset can behave like two phones with distinct apps, notifications, browsing history and file access.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Device-level identity separation is a native OS feature rather than a paid MDM add-on, capping the addressable market for third-party work/personal containerization apps.
insights.quote: It's essentially like having two phones on the same physical device
insights.locator: It's essentially like having two phones

insights.claim: The blurring of work and personal life on one device is framed as the core problem the feature solves, with the same phone delivering Slack pings from colleagues and Wordle scores from friends.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Consumer demand for boundary-setting tooling is a durable driver for both OS features and the productivity apps that sit on top of them.
insights.quote: The gadget that pings you on Slack when your colleague has a question is the same one that alerts you when your friend has just outscored you at Wordle. That blurring of boundaries can be a problem.
insights.locator: The gadget that pings you on Slack

insights.claim: Multi-user profile support has existed in Android for a long time and works on Pixel phones, but not every Android manufacturer has implemented it.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Feature fragmentation across Android OEMs means platform capabilities cannot be assumed device-wide, complicating enterprise deployment and app roadmaps.
insights.locator: Note that while this feature has been around

insights.claim: Samsung Galaxy phones do not offer Android's multi-user profiles and instead ship Samsung's own Secure Folder as a substitute.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Samsung continues to substitute proprietary equivalents for stock Android features, reinforcing its parallel software stack and its lock-in with users.
insights.quote: It's not available on Galaxy phones, for example, though Samsung does offer something similar with the Secure Folder.
insights.locator: Note that while this feature has been around

insights.claim: Files and apps in a second Android profile are not visible from the original profile or vice versa, so users needing to move files between them are advised to install a third-party cloud storage app.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Strict on-device isolation pushes cross-profile workflows into cloud storage services, creating incidental demand — and a data-governance gap — for those providers.
insights.quote: However, you won't be able to see saved files or apps in your second profile from your original one (or vice versa).
insights.locator: Some parts of the Android experience are shared

insights.claim: Profile isolation is not total: some parts of the Android experience, including Wi-Fi network information, are shared across profiles.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Shared system state means user profiles are a convenience boundary, not a full security boundary — relevant to anyone assessing BYOD risk.
insights.quote: Some parts of the Android experience are shared between profiles, including Wi-Fi network information.
insights.locator: Some parts of the Android experience are shared

insights.claim: Each Android profile is independently secured with its own PIN, fingerprint or face unlock, and an Allow user switch toggle on the primary account can temporarily disable switching without deleting the second account.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Per-profile authentication and switch controls are the practical building blocks device-management vendors must match or wrap.
insights.locator: On the Settings > System > Users screen

insights.claim: Setting up a work profile requires a second Google account, which can be created free of charge through the Google account portal with only a first name, birthday and desired Gmail address.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Google account creation remains the low-friction gateway into Android's feature set, extending Google's identity graph at zero marginal cost to the user.
insights.locator: To begin with, you're going to need two Google accounts
